request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Use fold-level evidence to decide: a config that wins a majority of folds is more trustworthy than one with a higher mean but inconsistent fold performance. Between two configs with similar fold-win rates, prefer the simpler model. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 1 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means one config clearly wins most folds and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means fold wins are split roughly evenly or something looks off. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run. Compare fold-by-fold: count how many folds each config wins to assess which is genuinely better vs lucky. (Independent run 3.)

concerns: Run 4 wins 4 of 5 folds (1, 3, 4, 5). Only fold 2 goes to run 1, by a hair (0.7304 vs 0.7295). Run 4 beats run 1 by 0.0085 mean PR-AUC, a small margin relative to the fold sd of about 0.066.

Fold-to-fold variation is large (fold 3 about 0.64 vs fold 4 about 0.81) and tracks across all configs. This suggests the folds differ in difficulty, or that the small positive count (about 500 flagged providers) makes PR-AUC noisy.

The PotentialFraud label has no documented origin, so it is suspicion rather than confirmed fraud. High PR-AUC (about 0.74) and ROC-AUC (about 0.946) may reflect the model learning the labelling process, or leakage from provider size or volume features, rather than true fraud.

Run 3, which drops size features and adds agent features, scores only about 0.03 lower than run 4. Run 2 (no_size random forest) is lower still. This suggests size features add modest signal and that much of the signal is not size-driven. Even so, ROC-AUC above 0.94 deserves scrutiny.

Claims cover only about 13 months, and the fold split is not described. If folds are not grouped or time-aware, there may be optimistic leakage. Precision@50 of about 0.79 is the more relevant operational number for a queue of about 100, and precision at 100 was not reported.
Class weighting did not help in run 3, and run 4 without imbalance handling is best. The calibration of the score for ranking has not been examined, but ranking is all the audit queue needs.
Only 4 configs were tried. Run 4 is a simpler, more regularized variant of run 1 and wins, which suggests that further tuning is likely to give only marginal gains within the noise.
